evidence.note: Genuine climax build: after both wrestlers reach TOP_ROPE, 'Hitman snaps off hurricanrana — Hall takes 22 damage.' plus 'Hall is rattled — when they're forced up, big payoffs may open.' sets up the cover two turns later.

The batch's only near-fall lands here and it is the high point of the match: 'Referee: 1… Referee: 2… Hall kicks out!' The menu had offered a real fork — cover ('pin') vs Sharpshooter (72%) vs Pull opponent up — so the kickout punishes a choice rather than a script.

Immediate follow-up keeps the arc alive: 'Hitman snaps off pull opponent up — Hall takes 3 damage.' / 'Hall is yanked up — their legs aren't under them yet!' converts the failed pin into a groggy window, which Hall then shakes off on T34.

Twelve-turn drag in the middle: from T17 to T28 every exchange is a reversal for 1–3 damage (T18, T20, T22, T24, T26, T28) while the player cycles Hit the ropes / Kill the run / Climb; health only moves 121→109 across twelve turns and no loop-tax warning ever fires on this cycle.

Finish has little buildup relative to length: Hall sits at 17 HP from T61 onward, the player spends T63 on 'Catch your breath' with the cover already legal, and the T65 pin is a clean three-count. 65 turns against a [8, 40] band.

Status changes are explicit and correctly modeled as a modifier: 'Hall is GROGGY — power moves and finishers are live!' with position STANDING and groggy=[false,true]; T13's menu then leads with 'TARGET GROGGY payoff: heavy damage is available now'.

Pin is visible and labeled honestly whenever legal ('Cover — pinfall attempt', note 'try to end it now; stronger when they're worn down'), and Sharpshooter is separately labeled 72% — consistent with the rule that the percentage is the chance to apply, not to win. curation_pin_visible=true.

Friction: RUNNING_ROPES offers exactly one option, 'Kill the run' (86%), and the same single-choice wall repeats at T23 and T25 (single_choice_turns=3). The T23 miss strands the player on the ropes for another dive attempt with nothing to decide.

Legibility gap in the loop feedback: the player repeats Kill the run three times and Hit the ropes twice while Hall repeats top-rope dives six times, yet none of the anti-loop lines ('The climb looks telegraphed', 'Another empty climb') ever fire, so the twelve-turn stalemate is never explained to the player.

Good chronology on the escape side: 'Hall tries to rise but can't find it — still down and vulnerable, but the crowd is pulling them up.' / 'Escape momentum builds for Hall.' matches state momentum 0→1 for Hall, so the drift after the kickout is readable.

The kickout leaves an obvious counterfactual to test: the same menu offered Sharpshooter at 72% and Pull opponent up, and the cover was taken instead — 'Hall kicks out!' directly invites replaying that decision.

Second distinct payoff route discovered late: 'Hitman snaps off missile dropkick — Hall takes 19 damage.' from a solo top-rope position, a different big swing from the T29 hurricanrana, so the top rope has more than one line worth exploring.

The rope-sprint branch is barely touched: Kitchen-sink knee (80%) hit for 15 and again for 15 on T61, while Rebound clothesline and Drop toe hold sat unused both times — a clear untested lane for another run.

stickiness.rematch_reason: The T31 kickout is the only near-fall in the batch and it changed the match's shape rather than ending it, and the position variety (position_diversity=9, move_repetition_rate=0.1212) meant most turns offered something new.
stickiness.next_experiment: Replay seed 229 and at T31 take Sharpshooter (72%) instead of the cover, then compare against a run that takes Pull opponent up into the T15/T37 'TARGET GROGGY payoff' suplex, to see which finish route produces a shorter match with the near-fall preserved.

evidence.note: Key juiciness datapoint — the batch's single near-fall. It is produced by hurricanrana (22 damage, T29) → failed get-up ('Hall tries to rise but can't find it — still down and vulnerable to a cover!', T30) → cover, resolving as 'Referee: 1…\n  Referee: 2…\n  Hall kicks out!' The finish_sequence carries delays_sec 1.0 and 1.5 before the kickout line and won=false, so the beat is paced, not instant.

The kickout pays off immediately instead of dead-ending: 'Hall is yanked up — their legs aren't under them yet!' turns the failed pin into a groggy window, and T34's 'Hall steadies themselves — they're back!' closes it.

Second impact spot with state shift: 'Hitman snaps off missile dropkick — Hall takes 19 damage.' plus 'Hall is rattled — when they're forced up, big payoffs may open.', cashed on T44 as 'Hall rises — still groggy from the impact!'

Repetition drags the ceiling down: 'Hitman reverses the diving crossbody — only 2 damage' appears three times (T18, T20, T22) and near-identical reversal text six times across T18–T28; log_uniqueness_ratio=0.6234.
Actual finish is flatter than the mid-match near-fall: same 1.0/1.5 delays but a plain 'Referee: 3!\n  *** PINFALL — Hitman wins ***' with no finisher heat or echo line preceding it.

top_issues.summary: A twelve-turn rope/top-rope stalemate (T17–T28) survives untouched because the loop tax does not cover it. Player cycles Hit the ropes → Kill the run → Climb while Hall repeats top-rope dives; six consecutive reversals deal 1–3 damage each and none of the anti-loop lines ('The climb looks telegraphed', 'Another empty climb') fire. This stretch is the main reason the match overshoots the [8, 40] band at 65 turns.
top_issues.suggested_area: Extend loop-tax coverage from tie-up/counter to the climb / hit_the_ropes / feet_plant cycle

top_issues.summary: Pacing gate fails at 65 turns even though tactical variety is high (move_repetition_rate=0.1212, position_diversity=9); the drag comes from reversal-heavy exchanges dealing near-zero damage rather than from move repetition, so repetition telemetry alone would not catch it.
top_issues.suggested_area: Damage floor or momentum consequence on repeated whiff/reversal exchanges

top_issues.summary: RUNNING_ROPES against a TOP_ROPE opponent curates down to a single option, 'Kill the run' (T19, T23, T25 — single_choice_turns=3), and a miss on T23 re-strands the player with the same lone choice.
top_issues.suggested_area: RUNNING_ROPES curation when the opponent holds the top rope

top_issues.summary: The near-fall at T31 is stronger than the actual finish at T65; the winning cover has no finisher heat, no echo line, and reuses the same delay pacing, so the match peaks 34 turns before it ends.
top_issues.suggested_area: Escalating finish text when a prior cover was kicked out
